flashcard_questions.q: Which paradoxical description does Dickens give the Ghost of Christmas Past?
flashcard_questions.a: “like a child: yet not so like a child as like an old man”

flashcard_questions.q: Which word means lasting for only a short time, not permanent or consistent?
What does the bright jet of light from the Ghost of Christmas Past symbolise?
flashcard_questions.a: Truth and enlightenment — the illumination of forgotten, buried memories.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Scrooge do to the spirit's light at the end of Stave 2?
flashcard_questions.a: He forces the extinguisher cap over it to suppress painful self-knowledge.

flashcard_questions.q: Which quotation describes young Scrooge left alone at boarding school?
flashcard_questions.a: “a solitary child, neglected by his friends”

flashcard_questions.q: Why is Scrooge weeping for his “poor forgotten self” a significant moment?
flashcard_questions.a: It is the first time the reader sees him cry, revealing buried pain beneath his coldness.

flashcard_questions.q: Which word means sentimental longing for a happier period in the past?
What does Fan promise young Scrooge when she comes to collect him?
flashcard_questions.a: To take him “home, for good and all. Home, for ever and ever.”

flashcard_questions.q: Whose mother was Fan, Scrooge's beloved sister?
What power does Fezziwig show an employer holds over their staff?
flashcard_questions.a: The power to “render us happy or unhappy; to make our service light or burdensome”.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does Dickens call Fezziwig the anti-Scrooge?
flashcard_questions.a: His warmth and generosity as an employer expose Scrooge's coldness by contrast.

flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by ‘pensive’, the word used as Scrooge watches Fezziwig's party?
flashcard_questions.a: Engaged in deep, serious thought or reflection.

flashcard_questions.q: What reason does Belle give for ending her engagement to Scrooge?
flashcard_questions.a: “Another idol has displaced me… a golden one.”

flashcard_questions.q: Which biblical sin does Belle's word “idol” allude to?
flashcard_questions.a: Worshipping a golden idol, like the Golden Calf in Exodus.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Belle mean when she tells Scrooge “You fear the world too much”?
flashcard_questions.a: His greed grows from fear — money feels safer to him than trusting people.

notes: 15 cards: 5 character or theme to quotation, 4 quotation-to-effect, 3 term-to-definition (ephemeral, nostalgia, pensive, all definition-front phrased as 'Which word means…' where the answer is one word), 2 symbol-to-meaning (the light, the extinguisher), 1 context card (Fan and Fred). Dropped 'knowledge' and 'foil' as glossary cards — 'knowledge' is flavour and 'foil' is already tested through the Fezziwig contrast card.
